## Overview

I built a Signal chatbot to explore what it takes to make a local language model useful in everyday messaging. The project connects Signal to Ollama while handling conversation state, group mentions, administrator commands, and the operational constraints of a shared Signal account.

The public edition generalizes that implementation into a configurable assistant. It includes a neutral persona and fictional example contacts; operators supply their own account details and model endpoint.

## How it works

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    Signal[Signal messages] --> CLI[Signal CLI in Docker]
    Setup[REST account registration] -.-> CLI
    CLI --> Router[Message routing and admin commands]
    Router --> Context[Conversation state and persona]
    Context --> Ollama[Local Ollama inference]
    Ollama --> CLI
    Router -. Think command .-> Search[Optional web search]
    Search --> Ollama
```

I registered a dedicated Signal account with its own phone number on the server using the REST API supplied by `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api`. The container's mounted account directory preserves the registration, keys, and sessions.

During normal operation, the host's Python application runs `signal-cli` receive/send commands inside that container through `docker exec`. The REST API provides the account setup path; message handling uses the CLI directly. A shared lock coordinates account access, and the deployment uses a non-daemon container mode without a competing automatic receiver.

Direct messages can trigger a reply immediately; group messages require a mention or command-prefix trigger. Replies use the incoming group ID automatically. Model requests go to Ollama's native `/api/chat` endpoint with conversation history, a text-based persona, and optional contact context.

The repository includes a standalone-account walkthrough for SMS/voice verification, bot service-ID discovery, manual transport checks, host/container paths, every environment setting, and lifecycle troubleshooting.

## Engineering decisions

- **Separate transport from inference.** Signal and Ollama clients sit behind distinct interfaces, allowing message routing and conversation logic to be tested with fake clients.
- **Coordinate concurrent work.** A semaphore bounds concurrent inference across conversations, per-conversation locks protect ordering, and a shared CLI lock prevents competing account operations. Pending replies take priority over another long receive call.
- **Bound conversation state.** History stays in memory, older exchanges are summarized, and idle state expires. Model, temperature, and mute settings can be overridden per chat.
- **Make behavior configurable.** Text templates define personas, optional role templates adjust tone, and an administrator command registry handles runtime controls.
- **Keep routine logs minimal.** Incoming-message logs record message type and length without message text or sender and group identifiers. Account data and local configuration are excluded from the source bundle.

The main integration challenge was coordinating a blocking CLI transport with asynchronous model work. The application uses worker threads for blocking calls and explicit locks for access to the Signal account.

## Validation and limits

The public implementation has **17 automated tests** covering message routing, administrator settings, state expiry, configuration, contact loading, search parsing, reply sanitization, cleanup, and default-persona loading. Tests use temporary fixtures and fake clients, so they do not require a live Signal account.

Local inference gives the operator control of the model endpoint, but the bot host still handles decrypted messages. Optional think-mode searches send queries to DuckDuckGo. Shutdown cleanup removes selected runtime data on a best-effort basis; it does not guarantee secure erasure. The source includes setup instructions and account diagnostics; a live deployment requires an operator-provided account and model server.

**Stack:** Python, asyncio, Ollama, Signal CLI, Docker, SQLite maintenance utilities, unittest.
